messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Error rate spike (5xx) on /v1/generate (redwood-hosted-us-west) — start=3412006740 count=120 rate=6.5%
alice_oncall: picking this up. seeing 5xxs coming from runtime-gpu-02 pool. any customer reports?
marta_support: getting a DM from ACME corp complaining of truncated responses and occasionally failed requests since ~13:30 PT. I asked for request ids.
raj_runtime: I can see a correlated increase in KV cache mismatch warnings in logs: "kvcache: seq_mismatch detected for key=conv-*-kv, expected_seq=4521 got=4499" repeated a lot around the same time.
sophia_sre: that smells like cache reuse with wrong seq offsets — maybe a new batch config landed?
james_enginfra: there was a deploy 13:25 PT touching continuous-batching defaults — we rolled a canary then.
alice_oncall: ok, let's treat as potential correctness issue causing cross-request leakage. Is there an easy mitigation? can we disable KV reuse or fall back to per-request caching?
raj_runtime: yes, we can toggle `enable_kv_reuse` at the runtime config to false for the affected pool. That will require rolling config to runtime-gpu-* nodes, but it's quick. Impact: ~5-8% higher token latency, fewer 5xxs if root cause is reuse.
sophia_sre: also we can disable the new batching window (max_continuous_batch_tokens=4096 -> revert to 2048) as a hotfix. Which is lower blast radius?
alice_oncall: disabling kv reuse first. Raj, can you push the config toggle and post command?
raj_runtime: running command now on k8s configmap: ```kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/enable_kv_reuse","value":"false"}]'```
incident-bot: Deploy job started: runtime-config-patch-3412006789 by raj_runtime.
raj_runtime: patch applied to configmap. triggering rolling restart (graceful) of runtime pods in pool runtime-gpu-02. ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-pool-gpu-02```
alice_oncall: monitoring error rate metric and logs.
~5min later~
alice_oncall: error rate dropped from 6.5% -> 1.1% in 4 minutes. 5xx counts still above baseline but trending down.
marta_support: ACME says errors stopped shortly after 13:35 PT. They reported some bad completions earlier; asked them to replay a few failing request ids.
kevin_custops: collecting request ids now, will pass along. Early customer impact: 3 major customers saw failures/garbled outputs for ~10 minutes.
sophia_sre: good mitigation. Need to confirm root cause: logs show seq_mismatch and occasional "kv_get() returned value for key belonging to different conversation". That indicates cross-request leakage rather than pure token loss.
raj_runtime: digging in to why the new batching window could have caused stale seqs. Hypothesis: the continuous batcher kept key references across micro-batches and reused kvcache entries while rolling seq number forward for one request but not updating associated metadata for others. We'll instrument additional asserts for key->seq boundaries.
james_enginfra: opened a short-lived feature-flag rollback PR for the batching change; recommending revert until we add stricter invariants.
alice_oncall: create an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime and eng-sre for a full postmortem. For now, keep `enable_kv_reuse=false` globally for runtime-gpu-02.
raj_runtime: set `enable_kv_reuse=false` cluster-wide for all GPU pools as precaution. ```kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/enable_kv_reuse","value":"false"}]' --all```
incident-bot: Configuration change detected: enable_kv_reuse=false applied cluster-wide by raj_runtime.
alice_oncall: rolling restarts done. Watching tail of logs for "seq_mismatch".
sophia_sre: running targeted grep across last 30m logs: seq_mismatch messages are down 96%.
marta_support: ACME confirmed they saw normal output after mitigation. Sent compensation note to account team.
kevin_custops: noting impacted customers: ACME (paying prod), BrightAnalytics (staging->prod leak observed), several smaller dev accounts with high concurrency. Will prepare customer impact summary.
alice_oncall: next steps: (1) keep kv_reuse disabled until root cause fixed and validated in canary, (2) rollback batching change or add safety guards, (3) add stronger kvcache asserts and end-to-end test that simulates overlapping conversation concurrency, (4) run a replay of captured failing requests in staging with dev flags.
raj_runtime: I'll add assert checks and a debug build that logs key->seq creation stack traces. Want to run on canary pool only.
james_enginfra: I will help instrument logging and prepare a small-scale canary for the revert.
sophia_sre: schedule follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT and include incident timeline, customer impact, and rollout decisions.
alice_oncall: handing off to raj_runtime for follow-up. I'm out in 40m — @sophia_sre you take next on-call watch and update incident doc.
sophia_sre: acknowledged, will take watch. created incident doc: https://docs.internal/incident/3412006789-kv-seq-mismatch (added initial timeline + mitigations)
raj_runtime: continuing root cause investigation. preliminary reproduce steps in local harness: run concurrent chat sessions with different seq progressions, enable continuous batching with window>3000 tokens, observe stale kv hits. I pushed a debug flag `kvcache_strict_mode=true` that aborts on mismatched seqs.
marta_support: any ETA to re-enable kv reuse? customers care about latency.
raj_runtime: need a fix + canary verification — estimate 4-6 hours to implement assertions + unit tests + canary runs. If tests pass, we can re-enable for canary only and monitor.
kevin_custops: I've drafted a short customer timeline + apology for affected accounts. Will share after the postmortem.
alice_oncall: thanks team. leaving final note: mitigation worked, customer impact contained to ~10–12 minutes for critical customers, root cause likely off-by-one seq bookkeeping combined with new batching window. Full RCA in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated — monitoring. owner=alice_oncall -> raj_runtime (handoff)
sophia_sre: added follow-up action items to incident doc: add end-to-end tests, telemetry counters for kv reuse hits, automatic circuit breaker if seq_mismatch rate > 0.1%
raj_runtime: will post updates in this thread as I progress. logs and debug snapshots uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/3412006789/
alice_oncall: last note before handoff — tag all PRs that revert batching change with "inc-3412006789" for traceability.
sophia_sre: acknowledged. I'll run a 2h watch starting now.
